paragraphs.en: Dorothy and her companions walked through dense woods, the yellow brick road now obscured by dead leaves and branches. Few birds sang in this part of the forest, as they preferred open areas with more sunlight.
paragraphs.zh: 多萝西和她的同伴们穿过茂密的森林，黄色砖路被枯叶和树枝遮掩得几乎看不清了。这片森林中很少有鸟儿歌唱，因为它们更喜欢阳光充足、开阔的地方。

paragraphs.en: Suddenly, a deep growl echoed from among the trees. Toto remained silent but close to Dorothy, sensing danger. The child asked the Tin Woodman how long it would take to reach the Emerald City.
paragraphs.zh: 突然，树林深处传来一声低沉的咆哮。托托保持沉默，但紧挨着多萝西，感受到了危险的气息。孩子问锡人木偶他们要多久才能到达翡翠城。

paragraphs.en: The Tin Woodman replied that he had never been there, but his father mentioned it was a perilous journey despite its beauty closer to Oz's city. He reassured them with his oil-can and the Scarecrow’s protection from harm due to Dorothy’s protective mark.
paragraphs.zh: 铁皮人回答说，他从未去过那里，但他的父亲曾提到，尽管通往奥兹城的这段路程美丽无比，却充满了危险。他用油罐给他们带来了安慰，并且由于多萝西的保护标记，稻草人也能免受伤害。

paragraphs.en: Dorothy worried about Toto’s safety. The Tin Woodman said they must protect him if needed.
paragraphs.zh: 多萝西担心托托的安全。铁皮人说，如果有必要，他们必须保护他。

paragraphs.en: Just then, a roar came from the forest, followed by a Lion bounding into their path. With one paw, the Lion knocked the Scarecrow off balance and lunged at the Tin Woodman with sharp claws. Surprisingly, he could not harm the tin figure.
paragraphs.zh: 就在这时，森林中传来一声吼叫，一只狮子跃入他们的路径。狮子用一只爪子将稻草人打了个趔趄，然后锋利的爪子向铁皮人扑去。令人惊讶的是，它无法对这个金属人造成伤害。

paragraphs.en: The Woodman fell but remained still.
paragraphs.zh: 樵夫倒下了，却一动不动。

paragraphs.en: Toto, now facing an enemy, barked fiercely. Before the Lion could bite him, Dorothy rushed forward, slapping the Lion’s nose hard. She shouted, "Don't you dare to bite Toto!
paragraphs.zh: 托托现在面对敌人，凶猛地叫了起来。狮子还没来得及咬他，多萝西已经冲了上来，狠狠地拍了一下狮子的鼻子。她喊道：“你敢咬托托！”

paragraphs.en: You're nothing but a big coward."
paragraphs.zh: 你不过是个胆小鬼罢了。

paragraphs.en: The Lion rubbed his nose and admitted, "I didn't bite him, but I tried."
paragraphs.zh: 狮子揉了揉鼻子，承认道：“我没咬他，但我试过了。”

paragraphs.en: The Lion hung his head in shame. "I know it. I've always known it, but how can I help it?"
paragraphs.zh: 狮子低下了头，羞愧不已。“我知道错了。我一直都知道，但这是怎么发生的呢？”

paragraphs.en: he asked.
paragraphs.zh: 他问道。

paragraphs.en: Dorothy picked up the Scarecrow and set him upright. "He's stuffed," she replied angrily. The Lion remarked, "That’s why he went down so easily.
paragraphs.zh: 多萝西拿起稻草人，让他站直了。“他只是塞满了稻草。”她生气地回答。狮子 then 说道：“这也就是他轻易倒下的原因。”

paragraphs.en: It astonished me to see him spin around like that." He then inquired about the other companion: "Is the Tin Woodman also stuffed?"
paragraphs.zh: 见到他转了这么一个圈，真是让我大吃一惊。“然后他又问起另一位同伴：‘铁皮木人也被填充了吗？’”

paragraphs.en: "No, he's made of tin," Dorothy explained as she helped the Woodman stand up.
paragraphs.zh: “不，他是用锡做的，”多萝西解释道，帮助樵夫站了起来。

paragraphs.en: The Lion continued, "That's why he nearly blunted my claws. The tin scratched against my back, causing a cold shiver." He then asked, "What about your little dog, Toto?"
paragraphs.zh: 狮子继续说道：“正因为如此，他差点磨钝了我的爪子。那罐头在我背上刮过，让我感到一阵寒意。”随后他又问，“至于你的小狗托托怎么样了？”

paragraphs.en: "He’s my dog," Dorothy answered. "Neither stuffed nor made of tin. He's just a meat dog."
paragraphs.zh: “他是我的狗，”多萝西回答说，“既不是填充玩具也不是锡制的。他就是一只普通的肉狗。”

paragraphs.en: The Lion sighed, "He seems remarkably small and curious. No one would bite such a tiny thing, except a coward like me."
paragraphs.zh: 狮子叹了口气，说道：“他看起来既小又好奇。这么个小东西，没人会咬它，除了像我这样的胆小鬼。”

paragraphs.en: Dorothy looked at the large beast in wonder. "What makes you a coward?" she asked.
paragraphs.zh: 多萝西惊奇地望着这只庞大的野兽。“是什么让你成了懦夫？”她问道。

paragraphs.en: "I don’t know," the Lion replied, wiping an eye with his tail. "I suppose I was born that way. All animals expect me to be brave because the Lion is thought to be the King of Beasts.
paragraphs.zh: “我不知道，”狮子回答着，用尾巴擦了擦眼睛。“大概就是天生这样的吧。大家以为我会很勇敢，毕竟狮子被认为是百兽之王。”

paragraphs.en: But whenever I meet a man, I’m scared and just roar at him; he always runs away."
paragraphs.zh: 但每次我遇到男人，我就害怕得直吼，他总是吓得逃之夭夭。

paragraphs.en: The Scarecrow interjected, "But the King of Beasts shouldn’t be a coward."
paragraphs.zh: 稻草人插嘴道：“可是兽王不应该胆小。”

paragraphs.en: The Lion agreed, "It’s my great sorrow, making my life unhappy. Whenever there is danger, my heart beats fast."
paragraphs.zh: 狮子同意道：“这是我最大的悲哀，让我的生活变得不快乐。每当有危险来临，我的心就会狂跳不已。”

paragraphs.en: The Tin Woodman said, "If you have a heart, you should be glad—it proves it exists. I have no heart, so I can't suffer from heart disease."
paragraphs.zh: 铁皮人说：“如果你有心脏，就应该感到高兴——这证明它还存在。我没有心脏，所以不会患上心脏病。”

paragraphs.en: The Lion pondered, "Perhaps without a heart, I wouldn’t be cowardly."
paragraphs.zh: 狮子沉思道：“或许没有了勇气，我反而不会这么胆小。”

paragraphs.en: "Have you brains?" asked the Scarecrow.
paragraphs.zh: “你有智慧吗？”稻草人问道。

paragraphs.en: "I suppose so," replied the Lion, "but I've never checked."
paragraphs.zh: “我想是吧，”狮子回答道，“但我从来没有核实过。”

paragraphs.en: "The Great Oz can give us what we need," said the Scarecrow. "He can provide me with brains and send Toto and me back to Kansas."
paragraphs.zh: “奥兹大王能够给我们提供我们需要的东西，”稻草人说道，“他可以给我提供智慧，然后送我们俩回堪萨斯州。”

paragraphs.en: "And he can give me a heart," added the Woodman.
paragraphs.zh: “他还能给我一颗心呢，”樵夫补充道。

paragraphs.en: "Or send you home," agreed Dorothy.
paragraphs.zh: “或者送你回家,”多萝西应道。

paragraphs.en: The Lion then said, "If he could grant courage as easily as brains, I'll join you. My life is unbearable without some courage."
paragraphs.zh: 狮子随后说道：“如果他能像赐予智慧那样轻易地给予勇气，我就会加入你们。没有一点勇气，我的生活简直无法忍受。”

paragraphs.en: Dorothy welcomed him, saying, "You’ll help keep away other wild beasts. They must be more cowardly than you to let you scare them so easily."
paragraphs.zh: 多萝西热情地迎接他，说道：“你来帮忙驱赶其他野兽。它们肯定比你更胆小，才会这么容易被你吓跑。”

paragraphs.en: "But that doesn’t make me braver," the Lion admitted. "Knowing myself a coward makes me unhappy."
paragraphs.zh: “但这并不能让我勇敢起来，”狮子承认道，“知道自己是个胆小鬼让我感到不快乐。”

paragraphs.en: With this, they set off again, the Lion walking proudly beside Dorothy. Toto initially disapproved but eventually became friends with the Cowardly Lion.
paragraphs.zh: 于是他们再次出发了，狮子昂首阔步地走在多萝西身旁。托托起初并不赞同，但最终还是与胆小的狮子成了朋友。

paragraphs.en: During the rest of that day, Dorothy and her companions traveled in peace, save for one incident. The Tin Woodman accidentally stepped on a beetle, killing it and causing him great sorrow. His tears rusted his jaw hinges, making him unable to speak.
paragraphs.zh: 在那天剩下的时间里，多萝西和她的同伴们平安地前行，只发生了一件事情。铁皮人不小心踩死了一只甲虫，这让他感到非常悲伤。他流下的眼泪腐蚀了他的下巴铰链，使他无法说话。

paragraphs.en: This puzzled both the Lion and Dorothy until the Scarecrow helped by oiling the Woodman's jaws.
paragraphs.zh: 这可难倒了狮子和多萝西，直到稻草人帮忙给樵夫涂上了润滑油。

paragraphs.en: The Tin Woodman learned from this experience: he must be careful not to harm any living creature, as crying would rust his jaws again. He began walking more carefully, avoiding even tiny ants. The Tin Woodman knew he lacked a heart and thus had no natural guide for right or wrong actions.
paragraphs.zh: 通过这次经历，锡头人明白了：他必须小心谨慎，以免伤害任何生物，因为哭泣会使他的嘴巴再次生锈。于是，他开始更加小心地行走，连小小的蚂蚁也不愿去碰。锡头人知道自己缺少一颗心，因此没有自然的道德指南来判断对错。

paragraphs.en: He stated that with a heart, people naturally do good; but without one, he must be extra cautious.
paragraphs.zh: 他说道：“有了良知，人们自然会做好事；但如果没有，他就必须格外小心。”
